entries.finding: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, VizieR V/137D/XHIP row HIP = 59803: position at J1991.25; Gaia cannot see the star. Distance: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 59803: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 21.23 +/- 0.2 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1134/S1063773712050015): 47.103 +/- 0.444 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star. Proper motion: VizieR V/137D/XHIP row HIP = 59803 (same row): -158.61, 21.86 mas/yr. entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 3.8 +/- 0.31 solar radii from Computed here, not printed by a paper: 3.8 +/- 0.31 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.75 +/- 0.06 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 21.23 +/- 0.2 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/167.1.121). No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 12450 +/- 530 K from Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 106625: effective temperature 12450 +/- 530 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared.

(1996, 1997), Baltic Astronomy 5, 603 and 6, 481; VizieR III/201. Gienah is HR 4662., cross-checked against Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 613: HR 4662; VizieR III/202 (4 levels apart at most, the threshold is 12), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #b1c8ff.
